articles.author: Matthew Trueblood
articles.take: Confirms the interest with his own source, then argues the Cubs have to take one big risk this winter and Duran is the cheapest version. The tools case from 2024 is real. But he lists Sato, Taira and Rogers as the other risks and never squares that the Cubs can't afford to spend a risk on a bat while the rotation is empty. The clubhouse-and-fans section is the most honest part of any Duran piece so far.
articles.title: Is Jarren Duran the Right Kind of Problem for Cubs to Try to Solve?

articles.author: Charlie Wright
articles.take: Clean on the fit: Sato is a third baseman behind Bregman, so he's a right fielder or DH here, and the 2026 DH at-bats are wide open. The Duran half is fair on the numbers (69 wRC+, 20 DRS in left since 2024). The call that Boston trades him rather than non-tenders him is the part to watch Friday. It also lists Duran as 28 when he's 30.
articles.title: Cubs Interested In Teruaki Sato, Jarren Duran

articles.author: Brett Taylor
articles.take: Takes Mooney's Duran report and asks the right question: is an $11M flyer plus a trade piece worth it when the staff is empty? His answer is no, and he's right. The best line is the prediction: Boston non-tenders him Friday and the Cubs can talk then. The Bellinger comparison is fair and he knocks it down himself.
articles.title: Another Jarren Duran Mention in Connection with the Cubs

articles.author: Matt Snyder
articles.take: A clean rumor roundup with useful scouting attached: Taira's extension and seven-pitch mix, and Sato's 66% contact rate against a 77% MLB average. It frames the Cubs right, pitching first. It doesn't push on the obvious problem: scouting a third baseman when Bregman is signed through 2030 is a DH plan at best.
articles.title: MLB rumors: Mets to meet with Japanese pitcher, plus latest on Cubs, Mariners, Nationals, more

articles.author: Michael Canter
articles.take: A good roundup of the week: Suzuki and the Padres, Gray, May, the Seattle trade, and the Silver Slugger/Gold Glove double. The frustration with Hoyer waiting for the market is earned. But it stops at mood. It never says which two arms to buy or what to pay, and the Taillon joke stands in for an actual plan.
articles.title: The Rundown (Pt 2): Hot Stove Heats Up, Padres Entertain Suzuki, Twins Sign Gray, Mariners & Royals Make Big Trade

articles.author: Anthony Franco
articles.take: Not a Cubs piece, but it's the most useful thing for Cubs fans this week. It lays out the exact mid-tier list the White Sox are shopping, and Taira and Rogers are on it. It also frames Rogers above $75M with pick cost. That makes the North Side's 'contacting everyone' approach look slower every day.
articles.title: White Sox Seeking Another Notable Starter After May Signing

body.h: Three doors closed in two days
p: On Monday the Cubs had a list. It had Dustin May on it, Sonny Gray on it, and a trade idea with Seattle for George Kirby or Emerson Hancock. By Wednesday night all three were gone.

May signed with the White Sox for three years and $52.5 million. Gray signed with the Twins for two years and $55 million. And the Mariners sent Bryce Miller and Logan Evans to Kansas City for Maikel Garcia, after which Jerry Dipoto said there's 'zero' chance Seattle trades another starter.

None of those is a disaster alone. May has a 4.70 ERA. Gray is 37 and his fastball fell to 91.5 mph. Kirby was never a sure thing. But put them together and the pattern is plain: the market is moving, and the Cubs are not in the reports when it moves.

body.h: The Seattle deal is the one that should sting
p: Seattle told everyone what it wanted: a right-handed bat, a third baseman or a left fielder. The Cubs have exactly that kind of surplus. Matt Shaw has a 102 OPS+ and no position. Pedro Ramírez held his own at 22, and the front office already plans to hand the corners to unproven guys.

Kansas City got there first. The Royals turned an infielder into two controllable starters and a lefty reliever. That's the move a front office makes when it treats the calendar as real. The Cubs had the pieces and the need, and they got beat by a team with less money and less urgency on paper.
Hancock threw 138 2/3 innings at a 3.57 ERA and was controlled through 2030. That's not an ace. It's a cheap No. 4 for four years, which is exactly the slot the Cubs can't fill.

body.h: Taira is now a four-team fight
p: The arm the Cubs clearly want is Kaima Taira, and the competition grew again. The Mets set a Zoom meeting. The White Sox, fresh off May, are openly looking for another notable starter and have Taira on the list. San Diego and Toronto were already in. MLBTR says he'll almost certainly sign within two weeks.

Taira is 26, threw 146 innings at a 1.36 ERA with a 24.8% strikeout rate, and sits 95-97. Bowden projected three years and $30 million. Bleacher Report's Zachary Rymer now has him going to the White Sox for four years and $68 million. That gap is the whole story. The early guesses were cheap, and the market is not going to be.

This is the one place the Cubs can't play their usual game. A posted player has a hard deadline. You can't wait out his price. If the Cubs think he's a mid-rotation starter, they have to pay like the Mets are in the room, because they are.

body.h: Suzuki leaving is fine. The money sitting is not.
p: Jeff Passan says the Padres met Seiya Suzuki on Monday and may be the favorite. Good. San Diego paying four years for a 32-year-old's 131 OPS+ is the clean ending: the Cubs collect a pick after the fourth round and keep the money.

But the money has to go somewhere. About $97 million came off the books. The projected 2027 tax payroll is around $169 million against a 2026 number of $265.6 million. Hawkins already said the corners might be filled with 'unproven guys' so they can buy 'more proven guys in other spots.' Those proven guys still don't exist, and two of them just signed elsewhere.

The lineup isn't the issue. The Cubs just became the first team to win the team Silver Slugger and the team Gold Glove in the same season. They lost a Wild Card sweep anyway, because Gausman lasted 3 1/3 innings and the bullpen blew 28 saves in the regular season. The best offense and best defense in the league aren't enough with a pitching staff held together by rehab dates.

body.h: The lockout makes the deadline real
p: Rob Manfred said Wednesday that MLB 'will not compromise' on a salary cap and floor. The union calls it a nonstarter. A Dec. 2 lockout is all but certain, and the last one went 99 days.

That changes the math on waiting. In a normal winter, the Cubs could let the middle tier settle and pick off a Peralta or a King in January. This winter, anyone they don't sign by Dec. 1 is probably unavailable until spring, and then they're shopping in a rushed market with every other team that waited.

Rymer predicts Freddy Peralta to the Cubs for six years and $130 million, built on the Counsell connection and the fact that Peralta carries no draft pick. That's a plausible guess. It's also just a guess, and nothing from the Cubs' side has moved it closer.
The Cubs need two real starters before Dec. 1, and the order matters. Taira first, because he has a deadline and the field is getting crowded. Then King or Peralta, whoever takes four years.

If they get both, this offseason is a B no matter what happens with Suzuki. If they get one, it's a C and the rotation leans on Steele's elbow and Cabrera's 5.96 ERA. If they get none, the Silver Sluggers and the MVP are going to look like the high point of a wasted window.
Twelve days. So far the only new name is Justin Lawrence. That's not a plan. It's Triple-A depth.

column.dek: May, Gray and the Mariners' trade door all closed this week without a Cubs bid on the record. Twelve days left, and the only addition is a reliever with a 5.34 career ERA.
column.title: The list is shrinking and the Cubs are watching it shrink

items.name: Pete Crow-Armstrong
items.note: Unanimous NL MVP. 45 HR, 41 SB, NL-best .942 OPS, MLB-best 10.6 fWAR. Hank Aaron Award, All-MLB First Team, Platinum Glove.

items.name: Seiya Suzuki
items.note: 131 OPS+, career-best 5.1 bWAR, Gold Glove finalist.

items.name: Alex Bregman
items.note: 5.8 bWAR, NL Gold Glove at third, All-MLB Second Team, ninth in MVP voting. Hitless in October.

items.name: Michael Conforto
items.note: 118 OPS+ on a minor-league deal.

items.name: Carson Kelly
items.note: 97 OPS+ and 1.9 bWAR from a catcher is a win.

items.name: Michael Busch
items.note: 106 OPS+ at first base. The walks carried him.

items.name: Ian Happ
items.note: 103 OPS+, 189 strikeouts, platooned by September.

items.name: Miguel Amaya
items.note: 98 OPS+, propped up by a .315 BABIP.

items.name: Pedro Ramírez
items.note: Held short together at 22. The xwOBA says he was lucky.

items.name: Nico Hoerner
items.note: 84 OPS+. The xBA says he deserved better; the glove is elite.

items.name: Matt Shaw
items.note: 102 OPS+ with a .303 xwOBA. Still looking for a position.

items.name: Dansby Swanson
items.note: His worst year as a Cub at the plate (90 OPS+). The glove saved the grade.

items.name: Ben Brown
items.note: 228 ERA+ over 68 innings before the neck gave out. Neck surgery Nov. 9; back around midseason.

items.name: David Peterson
items.note: 114 ERA+ after the June trade.

items.name: Shota Imanaga
items.note: 32 starts and a 112 ERA+. The 35 homers keep it from an A.

items.name: Matthew Boyd
items.note: 108 ERA+ in 22 starts, then two first-inning homers in Game 1.

items.name: Javier Assad
items.note: 3.63 ERA, 4.92 FIP. The defense did him favors.

items.name: Ryan Rolison
items.note: 135 ERA+ in middle relief from a waiver claim.

items.name: Colin Rea
items.note: 137 innings at a 97 ERA+. Exactly what he is.

items.name: Jacob Webb
items.note: Nine saves, eight blown.

items.name: Kevin Gausman
items.note: 4.83 ERA and 0.1 bWAR after the deadline deal.

items.name: Clay Holmes
items.note: 1.55 ERA over his first five starts, 8.24 over his last four.

items.name: Edward Cabrera
items.note: 71 ERA+, -1.4 bWAR, left off the Wild Card roster.

items.name: Jameson Taillon
items.note: 25 homers in 76 innings, -0.9 bWAR.

items.name: The bullpen
items.note: 28 blown saves, a third of inherited runners scored, 14 different save-getters.

items.name: Crow-Armstrong extension (6 yr, $115M)
items.note: The reigning unanimous MVP at about $19M a year through 2032. The best contract in baseball.

items.name: Bregman signing (5 yr, $175M)
items.note: 5.8 bWAR in year one. Years four and five are the risk.

items.name: Conforto minor-league deal
items.note: 118 OPS+ for almost nothing.

items.name: Peterson trade
items.note: 114 ERA+ in 15 starts.

items.name: Hoerner extension (6 yr, $141M)
items.note: Paying a glove-first second baseman through his age-35 season.

items.name: Gausman trade
items.note: A deadline splash worth 0.1 bWAR.

items.name: Cabrera trade (Caissie + 2)
items.note: The No. 1 prospect for 80 innings of 5.96 ERA.

items.name: Holmes trade (Rojas)
items.note: A top-two prospect for nine starts, zero postseason innings, and he opted out.

items.name: Bullpen construction
items.note: Hoyer's own words: 'I did a poor job on the bullpen this year, full stop.'

items.name: Kelly option declined ($1.5M buyout)
items.note: The right call on a mutual option. It only stays a B if they re-sign him or find a real starter.

items.name: Suzuki qualifying offer
items.note: Paid off as planned: he rejected it Tuesday, so the Cubs get a pick after the fourth round when he signs elsewhere.

items.name: No QO for Happ
items.note: He'd likely have taken $23.15M. Saying no was the disciplined call.

items.name: No QO for Boyd
items.note: A 36-year-old No. 5 isn't worth the risk of an acceptance.

items.name: Rea, Harvey, Thielbar options declined
items.note: $2.5M in buyouts to clear three arms that didn't miss bats or didn't pitch.

items.name: Assad option declined ($3.3M)
items.note: Saves about $1M through arbitration and keeps a useful swingman. Small, correct, and an honest read of a 4.92 FIP.

items.name: Webb restructure
items.note: Same $2.5M guarantee and a 2028 option. Smart, small.

items.name: Orze waiver claim
items.note: A 5.66 ERA with no options left. A free look, nothing more.

items.name: Sitting out Skubal (per Sharma)
items.note: $97M came off the books and the answer is 'we can't match the Dodgers.' It becomes a C only if King or Peralta and a trade arm land before Dec. 1.

items.name: Internal plan for LF, RF and C (per Hawkins)
items.note: Hawkins admits the risk: unproven corners to pay for 'proven guys in other spots.' Fine as a trade-off. It stays a C- until those proven guys exist.

items.name: Kanzler replaced (Ben Martin, farm director)
items.note: Fast, internal and sensible. Adding Rylan Domingues on the pitching-analytics side is the right department.

items.name: Wiggins, McCullough added to the 40-man
items.note: Protects the Detmers trade chip and a Double-A arm with a 27.7% K rate. Correct and routine.

items.name: This offseason so far
items.note: Option calls and QOs mostly right, zero real additions, a public pass on Skubal. Two linked starters (May, Gray) signed elsewhere this week, and Seattle traded its spare starters to Kansas City instead. The only signing is a likely minor-league deal for Justin Lawrence. Twelve days to the lockout.

items.name: Holmes reunion interest (per Hawkins)
items.note: They traded a top prospect for nine starts, he opted out, and the GM wants him back at a projected three years. Only a one-year swingman deal gets this off a D.

items.name: Justin Lawrence (likely minor-league deal)
items.note: Free Triple-A depth with a 5.34 career ERA and a walk problem. Harmless, and not the impact arm.

items.name: Missing the Mariners' starter sale
items.note: Seattle wanted a third baseman and a right-handed bat, the Cubs had both to spare, and Kansas City got Miller and Evans. Dipoto now says 'zero' more.

items.name: McDermott waiver claim
items.note: Free, uses an empty roster spot, 30.5% minor-league K rate. Also a 14.6% walk rate and no options. Depth, not help.

regressionNotes.663538: The one regular who was unlucky. A .296 xBA says the average comes back.
regressionNotes.664023: Small gap. The .218 is mostly him.
regressionNotes.665795: xFIP says unlucky; an 8th-percentile xERA says hitters crushed him. Don't bank on a big bounce.
regressionNotes.665804: A .315 BABIP for a catcher. Expect the OBP to slip.
regressionNotes.669020: Middle-relief ERA, back-end peripherals. Fine in low leverage.
regressionNotes.673548: The expected line is still well above average. Price him on that, not the surface numbers.
regressionNotes.676962: Still very good, just not 228-ERA+ good.
regressionNotes.691718: Even after the haircut, a .372 xwOBA is elite.
regressionNotes.699393: The largest gap on the team. Don't pencil him into a corner spot off this line.
